commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Warn about prefixes inside names and gig titles
commitResults.messageBody:
A prefix such as a/ or t/ inside a client name, or f/ inside a gig
title, starts a new field. Some commands then save the wrong fields
without an error. For example, `edit 1 n/Muthu a/l Raju` overwrites
the client's address with `l Raju`. The UG doesn't mention this, and
the planned upper-case workaround (`A/L`) doesn't work, because
names can't contain /.

Let's document the behaviour instead of changing the parser during
the feature freeze:

* State the name rule in the add section
* Add cautions to the add, edit, addgig and editgig sections
* Point to them from the command format notes and Known issues

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Document emoji title length and running two copies
commitResults.messageBody:
Two limitations are not mentioned in the UG, so users hit them
without warning:

* Running two copies of Gigabyte from the same folder loses changes.
  Each copy saves its own data after every command, so even `list`
  in one copy overwrites what the other added.
* Emoji count as more than one character toward the 100-character
  gig title limit, so a title of 51 emoji is rejected.

Let's add both to Known issues, and note the emoji rule where the UG
describes the title limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Remove AB3's proposed undo/redo section
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG still has AB3's proposed undo/redo section, with only the
class names changed, and the nine diagrams it uses. It describes
AB3's design rather than work done for Gigabyte, so PE testers may
report it as copied content.

Let's remove the section and the diagrams that only it uses. The
undo user story stays, marked as not implemented, and the team's own
proposed data archiving section remains.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Fix setup and wording in manual testing
commitResults.messageBody:
The manual testing appendix has three problems PE testers may report:

* The preparation note asks testers to build the JAR with gradlew,
  but they only get the released JAR.
* One expected result writes a payment as $1200.00, while the app
  shows $1,200.00.
* The v1.3 save file test says "Expected for the current release
  candidate" and calls the behaviour "a release compatibility gap",
  which reads like an admitted unfinished feature.

Let's tell testers to use the released JAR, match the app's money
format, and state the v1.3 behaviour plainly as a documented
limitation.

commitResults.messageTitle: SettingUp.md: Require JDK 25 instead of JDK 17
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup guide tells developers to configure IntelliJ with JDK 17,
but build.gradle targets Java 25 and the UG and DG both require Java
25. A developer following the guide cannot build the project.

Let's update the guide to ask for JDK 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Correct where log files are written
commitResults.messageBody:
The Data file format section says log files are kept in the JAR
folder. LogsCenter opens gigabyte.log with a relative path, so logs
go to the working directory the app is launched from. Only the data
and preferences files are resolved against the JAR folder.

Let's say that the JAR folder is the base for the data and
preferences files only, and state where log files are written.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add v1.5 and v1.6 work to the Effort appendix
commitResults.messageBody:
The Effort appendix describes only the features up to v1.4. None of
the v1.5 and v1.6 additions, such as keyboard navigation and save-file
backups, are mentioned.

Let's
* list the user-visible v1.5 and v1.6 additions under Achievements
* add the hard parts of the save-file backup, keyboard navigation and
  duplicate-client checks to Challenges faced

Warnings for similar client names are not listed, as that change was
not merged. Only the same-phone and same-email notes are in v1.6.

commitResults.messageTitle: Diagrams: Remove stale labels from DG diagrams
commitResults.messageBody:
The LogicClassDiagram note names "v1.4" commands, which is out of
date. The architecture sequence diagram calls deleteClient(p), a name
left over from AB3's Person.

Let's drop the version from the note and rename the argument to c so
it fits Client.

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Fix wording, spelling and punctuation
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG has a few small errors:
* Clement's GitHub username is written `approxneo` instead of
  `ApproxNeo`.
* "They were also used" refers to a single tool.
* An expected result in the manual tests ends with a double period.
* "prioritise" uses British spelling, while the rest of the DG and
  AB3 use American spelling.

Let's fix these so the DG reads correctly and uses one spelling
convention.

commitResults.messageTitle: AboutUs: Replace placeholder email with issue tracker link
commitResults.messageBody:
The About Us page lists gigabyte[at]comp.nus.edu.sg as the team's
contact. This line was carried over from the AB3 template and is not a
real mailbox, so readers who use it get no reply.

Let's point readers to the team's GitHub issue tracker instead, which
the team does monitor.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove outdated Configuration page and link dev guides
commitResults.messageBody:
Configuration.md says the app reads settings from config.json, but
Gigabyte no longer has a Config class or a config.json file. The page
is not linked from anywhere, yet it is still published and shows up
in site search. DevOps.md and Documentation.md are also published but
not linked from the DG, even though the DG section title mentions
documentation and dev-ops.

Let's,
* delete Configuration.md
* link the Documentation and DevOps guides from the DG's
  "Documentation, logging, testing, dev-ops" section, ordered to match
  the section title

commitResults.messageTitle: GigListPanel: Number gigs in the client's gig list
commitResults.messageBody:
Client and payment rows show their index, but gig rows do not. Users
must count gigs by hand to find the index that gig and payment
commands need.

Let's prefix each gig in a client's gig list with its one-based index,
matching the payment panel.

The gigs, deadlines and findgig views mix gigs from several clients,
and their row positions are not gig indexes. Numbering those rows
would point users at the wrong gig, so they stay unnumbered.

Two passages still describe the code from before indexed lookups were
centralized in CommandUtil. The per-client index section says
setstatus filters the gig list itself, but it now uses
CommandUtil#getGig like every other gig command. The Model component
lists CommandUtil, which lives in gigabyte.logic.commands, and several
other Logic and UI classes that the Implementation sections already
cover.

Let's,
* remove the setstatus special case
* describe CommandUtil in the per-client index section, with the
  commands that use it
* keep the Model component to classes in gigabyte.model
Remove outdated Configuration page and link dev guides

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Fix logging location and wording inconsistencies
commitResults.messageBody:
Logging.md says log files are written to the folder containing
gigabyte.jar. LogsCenter opens gigabyte.log with a relative path, so
logs go to the working directory the app is launched from. The README
description also differs from the home page, and Clement's About Us
responsibilities mix capitalisation.

Let's,
* describe the log location as the working directory
* reuse the home page wording in the README description
* use sentence case for the About Us responsibilities

A merge kept the code that treats a phone prefix after an address as
address text, undoing the fix from 33baac40. Phones given after an
address are silently saved into the address, and four parser tests
fail.

Let's restore the tokenizer to its version in 33baac40, so a phone
prefix after an address starts a phone field again.
Docs: Fix logging location and wording inconsistencies
ArgumentTokenizer: Restore phone after address

commitResults.messageTitle: ClientListCard: Wrap long names, addresses and emails
commitResults.messageBody:
Client cards cut off long names, addresses and emails with an
ellipsis, so the user cannot see the full value anywhere in the client
list. An ordinary Singapore address is already long enough to hit this
at the default window size.

The gig and payment rows already wrap their text, so they do not have
this problem.

Let's set wrapText on the name, phone, address and email labels so the
card grows taller to fit the full text. Let's also add a test that
renders a card at the client list's minimum width and checks that no
label is cut off.

commitResults.messageTitle: Phone: Limit phone numbers to 15 digits
commitResults.messageBody:
Phone numbers accept any number of digits, so a 200-digit number is
saved without complaint. The ITU-T E.164 standard limits international
numbers to 15 digits, including the country code, so a longer number
is almost certainly a typo.

Let's reject phone numbers with more than 15 digits, following the
pattern Tag uses for its length limit:

* Add Phone#isWithinDigitLimit, which counts digits only, so '+',
  spaces and hyphens do not count
* Check it in ParserUtil#parsePhone, which add and edit use
* State the limit in the error message and the User Guide

The limit is not checked when loading the data file, so a file saved
by an older version with a longer number still loads instead of
being discarded.
Fix overdue date boundary in developer guide

commitResults.messageTitle: HelpWindow: Restore the window if it is minimized
commitResults.messageBody:
Running help again while the Help window is minimized does nothing
visible, as HelpWindow#focus() only calls requestFocus(), which does
not restore a minimized window. The UG lists this as a known issue.

Let's un-minimize the window and bring it to the front before
requesting focus, and remove the entry from Known issues in the UG.
HelpWindow: Restore the window if it is minimized
Phone: Limit phone numbers to 15 digits
ClientListCard: Wrap long names, addresses and emails
DeveloperGuide: Describe CommandUtil under Logic

commitResults.messageTitle: DeveloperGuide: Update wording for unnumbered gig rows
commitResults.messageBody:
Since gig rows in the cross-client views lost their numbers, one
sentence still describes them as display-only numbers, and a manual
test asks testers to pick a gig by its position in such a view.

Let's describe the rows as they now appear, name the gig in the test,
and fix a typo in the documentation guide.
DeveloperGuide: Update wording for unnumbered gig rows

The User Guide has a few small inconsistencies with the rest of the
docs and with the app:

* The introduction says "projects", but the README and home page
  say "gigs"
* The edit format uses p/PHONE, but add and the command summary use
  p/PHONE_NUMBER
* The deletepayment success message is for deletepayment 1 1 1, not
  for either example above it
* The command summary has no space after "e.g.," for edit

Let's fix them, using the message that deletepayment 1 2 1 shows on
fresh sample data.

commitResults.messageTitle: UserGuide: Warn about prefixes inside addresses
commitResults.messageBody:
A prefix inside an address starts a new field, as it does inside a
name or gig title. With add, " t/" inside an address silently adds a
tag. With edit, " n/", " p/", " e/" and " t/" inside a new address
silently change those fields, e.g. "edit 1 a/Unit 5 n/a" renames the
client to "a". The User Guide only mentions " p/", in a general note.

Let's document it next to the other prefix cautions:

* Extend the command format note to all four prefixes
* Add a caution to add, and extend the caution in edit
* Extend the Known issues entry

Writing the prefix in uppercase, e.g. T/, keeps it in the address.
